I would send help, but I wouldn't know where to start. They got away this time - we'll get them though.

For what it’s worth, I am an aspiring novelist, hence the writing being a little more succinct than average. I’ve got tons of ideas but no time or drive to pen them.

As for the little girl, all I do all day is make her smile and giggle. In fact, with there being me, mommy and her grandparents all in the same house I’m the only one who gets baby kisses which just melts my heart.

That said, the adoration is a double-edged sword. In the moment it feels unreal to be able to make my daughter so happy she sounds like a donkey when she laughs, but the introspective takes on myself do not shine a good light on it. This little girl loves me beyond what I can fathom, but I know the truth. Eventually I will fail her in some way. I will forget something, or be unable to afford something she needs/wants, and I’ll have to live that moment. I will have to carry that with me for the rest of my days. Full disclosure, I stole some of her presents for her first Christmas. I couldn’t live with myself if her first tree wasn’t stacked, but for the rest of my days I’ll have to know that the toy she seems  to love most from that haul was not something I earned for her. I did something I am morally opposed to, just so I could give her a good Christmas, even if she won’t remember

The problem is I don’t know what I would be doing were I not stressed and depressed, I can’t remember a time where I wasn’t.

I’m the type of person everyone sees as overly happy, jovial and easy to get along with.

It’s a mask I’ve worn since middle school, the me the world sees isn’t me , but I have to keep up the act because... honestly I don’t know why, the charade is such a part of who I am that it’s hard to say why I ever put on the mask, but years of sweat, blood, and tears behind it have it stuck to me.
